narrative:
The model determined that you have a 27% chance of representing a bad credit risk. While this is not an extremely high probability, it was enough for the bank to deny your loan application.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this decision were your savings account status, your employment situation, and the length of the loan you requested. Your lack of any savings was the single biggest reason for the denial. Most approved applicants have at least some money set aside; because you have none, the model saw this as a significant warning sign that pushed the prediction strongly toward bad credit risk.

Your current unemployment also worked against you, though to a lesser degree. Only about 7% of approved customers are unemployed, so this status added further concern. Finally, the 48-month duration you requested is more than twice as long as the average loan length among people who are approved. Longer loans increase risk in the bank's view, so this factor also nudged the prediction toward denial.

Taken together, these three elements outweighed the positive aspects of your profile, such as your clean credit history and stable age.

To improve your chances next time, focus on building up savings, securing stable employment, and considering a shorter loan period if possible. Addressing these areas should meaningfully improve how future applications are viewed. (218 words)
